title: Replace a car headlamp's H11 bulb: unlatch its connector, quarter-turn the old bulb out, lock the new one in by its base
context: Replacing a burnt-out headlight bulb is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (about 700,000 in the US) and quick-lube and parts-counter staff. The bulb's connector has to be unlatched before it comes off, the bulb turned out of and into its bayonet port by its plastic base, and the new bulb's quartz glass must not be touched: skin oil on it makes a halogen capsule fail early. It is done with the lamp in place: reached past the radiator support and air box, the connector held on its short leads while the bulb is swapped.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m; everything is real size. The bench carries a real-size section of a compact car's front engine bay, cut at the bench (the bench stands for the bay floor), into which the headlamp is bolted as installed: a black e-coated steel upper radiator support (hat channel 275 x 50 x 30 mm) with an aluminium radiator core (210 x 22 x 195 mm) and black PA end tank below it on the lamp's inboard side (x -0.06 to 0.17, y 0.10 to 0.16); a silver-painted steel fender apron (470 x 260 mm, 4 mm, with a 46 mm top bolt rail) on its outboard side at x 0.64; and a black PP air-filter box (150 x 180 x 150 mm, four steel lid clips, 32 mm intake snorkel along the fender) beside the lamp's back at x 0.47 to 0.62, y -0.31 to -0.13. The headlamp is a halogen reflector unit of the H11 low beam / 9005 high beam type (400 W x 200 H x 250 D mm, 1.6 kg; black polypropylene housing, clear polycarbonate lens wrapping round its outboard corner over an aluminised turn-signal reflector, two blue beam adjusters), lens toward +y, back face at y -0.06 toward the right arm, bolted by three M6 flange bolts through its steel-bushed ears to black steel brackets on the radiator support (x 0.20, y 0.04), the fender (x 0.58, y 0.04) and a lower support (x 0.57, y 0.0). On its back, two moulded ports 115 mm above the bench: the high-beam port (x 0.47) keeps its black rubber dust cover (62 mm); in the low-beam port (x 0.33; 36 mm bore, boss 48 mm across) sits the old H11 12 V 55 W bulb (PGJ19-2 base with three bayonet lugs, grey PBT grip, 10 mm quartz capsule, 25 g), locked, its L-shaped socket toward the arms (-x), with the lamp's black PA66 pigtail connector (22 x 18 x 22 mm) latched onto it. The connector's grey latch tab (15 x 11 x 3 mm) is a sprung key on its top (2 mm travel). Its two 18 AWG leads, taped together (5 mm across, about 160 mm), run back 44 mm, down 85 mm and 32 mm forward to a harness clip low on the lamp's back (x 0.235, y -0.071, 30 mm up), whence a 13 mm corrugated loom runs to the radiator support. The new H11 bulb (same part) lies in its opened blister pack (blue printed paperboard card 110 x 160 mm, clear PETG tray, lid torn back) on the bench at x 0.225, y -0.30: axis along +y, capsule toward +y, socket down into the tray, flange in the tray's moulded cradle.
scoring: 0.25: the old bulb is out: turned its quarter turn back, withdrawn at least 20 mm off its seat (a milestone, kept once reached) and still at least 15 mm away, wherever it was set down. 0.5: and the new bulb is locked in the port: put in square and turned at least 88 degrees. 0.75: and the connector is latched on the new bulb's socket. 1.0: and every finger pad's surface is at least 80 mm from the new bulb's and the connector's surfaces and 50 mm from the old bulb's, the old bulb at rest (under 0.02 m/s and 0.2 rad/s), held 1 s. Touching the new bulb's glass caps the score at 0.5 -- in a real trial, any frame of the wrist or overview videos showing a finger on the capsule; in simulation, any finger pad's surface within 2.5 mm of it; a bulb or the connector falling off the bench scores 0.
reset_notes: Fixed poses, no randomisation: the old bulb locked in the low-beam port with the connector latched on it, the new bulb in its blister; the arms at their rest poses.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz; parts rigid, detailed meshes over simple hidden colliders. The latch tab is a sprung key (3.5 kN/m) that must be pushed down 1.2 mm (about 4 N) for 0.2 s to free the connector; the leads are 7 colliding capsule links on sprung D6 joints from the connector to the harness clip. Each bayonet is a port-axis hinge held by stops and damping, the new bulb's switched on when put in square and locked at 88 deg; the connector latches within 4 mm of its seat.
